title.narrative: Food production support and integrated multi-sector emergency services in Ar Rahad and Sheikan, North Kordofan.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project will be implemented in North Kordofan in both Sheikan and Ar Rahad localities. In coordination with OCHA and the clusters, SCI in partnership with GPBC will be implementing health, nutrition, food security and livelihoods and child protection. This will be also in coordination with other actors such as LMI and AORD who are also implementing OCHA funded projects in the state as well. North Kordofan is indirectly affected by the on-going security and conflict situation in Darfur and the protracted situation in South Kordofan.ltbrgtSheikan has high number of IDPs that came in from neighboring localities due to the ongoing conflict is the state and put strain on already fragile context within Sheikan locality. According to the DTM report (Jan 2025), an estimated 90% of displaced households reportedly needed food (90%), livelihoods (59%), healthcare (51%). Ar Rahad is a locality that is controlled mostly by RSF and has been struggling from the lack of commodities entering the locality and the community has no option of moving anywhere else, and their health and nutritional status is deteriorating and its IPC 4 rated. Children and women in North Kordofan also face severe protection risks driven by conflict (including inter-communal clashes), compounded by natural hazards, climate change, and environmental degradation. Children’s vulnerabilities are shaped by gender, age, and disability. Girls face the highest risks of GBV, forced marriage, and sexual exploitation, while boys are more likely to experience forced recruitment, detention, or child labour. Adolescents endure psychological distress due to instability and violence, while children with disabilities remain marginalised, with systemic barriers limiting their access to services and protection. The root causes of these risks leave children exposed to exploitation, child labour, and forced recruitment. Families forced into harmful coping mechanisms, such as child marriage and survival sex, perpetuate cycles of poverty and abuse.ltbrgtSCI and GBPC will be providing lifesaving services, benefiting a total of 35,978 individuals, including 16,029 IDPs. GPBC will provide supporting 2 health facilities in Ar Rahad locality. Health and nutrition activities will be implemented in those facilities, where Primary Health Care PHC will be provided to the local community, serving 19,256 individuals (5,893 women, 3,928 girls, 5,661 men, 3,774 boys). With the technical guidance of SC, GPBC will implement the Assida Plus approach to prevent malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating in Ar Rahad. Nutrition interventions will benefit 4,362 individuals. ltbrgtSCI will be leading the implementation of Child Protection and FSL components in Sheikan locality. The program will create synergies with ongoing SC programmes, including SHF activities in health and nutrition. The FSL activities will be focused on improving agricultural practices and increasing food production for 3,560 farmers, and the improvement of animal health services for 2,500 livestock. This should bolster and enhance the community's ability to provide for their nutritional needs and maintain their livelihood. The protection activities will focus on providing protection services for those at risk by comprehensive case management for children, establishing Child Friendly Spaces, conducting MHPSS activities, establishing and reactivating 2 Community-Based Child Protection Networks and increase their capacity to respond to the protection needs of girls and boys. In Addition, SC will establish 2 women support groups for Community Mobilization and GBV Prevention and Response, Focusing on Early Child Marriage, FGM, and Sexual Violence. The protection activities will cover (3000 Women, 2100 Girls, 2000 Men, 1700 Boys) to a total of 8,800 beneficiaries.ltbrgtlt/pgt
